members.name: Antarctic Air Temperature 2005-07-01
members.description: Air temperature over Antarctica on 1 July 2005. Values are in tenths of a degree Celsius, so -300 on the legend is -30 ℃; the legend runs from -900 to 0.

members.name: GIA Anomaly
members.description: Glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) anomaly, in metres. GIA is the slow rise and fall of the bed as the solid Earth responds to changes in ice load. The legend is in 200 m bands from below -800 m to above 800 m.

members.name: GIA Global Bed Topography
members.description: Bed topography from a glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) model run, identified by its file name as mv1e21_fr1e24_w0p0_weakEarth_t20. In metres, with the legend from -1000 m to 1000 m.

members.name: Lowry2024 Ice Sheet Model
members.description: Output of the Lowry 2024 ice sheet model at 9.5 ka (9,500 years ago), run ism_hotf0-0_mv7-5e20_fr1e24. In metres, with the legend from 0 m to 4500 m. Click a point on the layer to chart modelled ice thickness there over the model's time steps, one line per model run.

members.name: PSKRIPS Wind Speed 2017-02-01
members.description: Daily mean wind speed 10 m above the surface on 1 February 2017, from PSKRIPS model output. In metres per second, from 0 m/s (dark purple) to 24 m/s (yellow). Derived from the U and V wind components as sqrt(u^2 + v^2).

members.name: PSKRIPS Wind Arrows 2017-02-01
members.description: Daily mean wind 10 m above the surface on 1 February 2017 as arrows, from PSKRIPS model output. Each arrow points the way the wind blows and is coloured by speed in metres per second. Overlay it on the wind speed layer, or use it on its own.

members.name: PSKRIPS Atmosphere Daily Mean in Celsius 2017-02-01
members.description: Daily mean air temperature on 1 February 2017, from PSKRIPS model output. In degrees Celsius, with the legend from -30 ℃ to 0 ℃.

members.name: PSKRIPS Atmosphere Daily Mean in Kelvin 2017-02-01
members.description: Daily mean air temperature on 1 February 2017, from PSKRIPS model output. In kelvin, with the legend from 243.15 K to 273.15 K. The same field as the Celsius layer.

members.name: tankersley Sediment thickness 2023
members.description: Thickness of sediment beneath Antarctica, from the Tankersley 2023 dataset. In metres, with the legend from 0 m to 4500 m.

members.name: Ice thickness blocks: band 9, Ross Sea POC
members.description: Experimental 3D columns derived from ice_ds.nc thk band 9. Thickness is rounded upwards into 250 metre classes and positioned on the ETOPO surface. Column height is illustrative and does not represent a reconstructed physical ice surface.

catalog.name: Sea ice forecast
catalog.description:
What this shows

An 8-week forecast of sea ice concentration around Antarctica, one map per week. Concentration is the fraction of each 1-degree cell covered by sea ice, from 0 (open water) to 1 (fully covered). The legend shows it as a percentage, and cells below 1% are left clear.

How it is made

The forecast comes from a graph neural network by Tobias Milz. It is driven by ECMWF ERA5 data (10 m wind, 2 m air temperature, mean sea level pressure, total precipitation and sea surface temperature) and NSIDC sea ice concentration, taken from the most recent four weeks. A new forecast is made every Monday, and each map is titled with the date of its week.

How to use it

Open the process below, choose a week and run it to add that week's map. Click a point on the map to chart all 8 weeks at that point.

Known limits

The pole hole reads as 0.

members.name: Sea ice concentration forecast
members.description: Map one week of the newest 8-week sea ice concentration forecast, then click the map to chart all 8 weeks at that point. Please click the parent 'Sea ice forecast' folder for a detailed description.
